title: Company-wide policies and processes — Access, Change, Data, Procurement, Vendors, Travel & Templates
author: Alyssa Chen
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and internal templates. It is intended to be the canonical reference for employees, managers, and reviewers. Owners and contact points are listed per section.

Scope and goals
- Provide clear, auditable processes that meet security, finance, and compliance requirements.
- Reduce cross-team friction by standardizing request/approval flows.
- Preserve least privilege and data protection while enabling developer productivity.

Owners and escalation
- Primary owner: People Ops (people-ops).
- Security owner for access/data controls: Security & Compliance (security-and-compliance).
- Finance owner for procurement and expense rules: Finance & Legal (finance-legal).
- For operational issues escalate to: ops-escalation@redwood.ai (see escalation-playbook).

1) Access & Permissions

Purpose
Ensure consistent, least-privilege access to systems, cloud accounts, data stores, and vendor consoles.

Roles & responsibilities
- Team leads: approve role-level access for direct reports.
- System owners: approve service-specific access and review quarterly.
- Security: manage privileged role definitions, run access reviews, and enforce MFA & SSO.

Permission model (summary table)
| Role | Typical scope | Approval required | Review cadence |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| Viewer | Read-only dashboards, docs | Team lead | 90 days |
| Contributor | Modify infra/app resources (non-prod) | Team lead + system owner | 60 days |
| Service Account | Programmatic access scoped to a service | Sys owner + Security | 30 days |
| Admin | Full control (prod infra, billing) | Director + Security + Finance | 30 days |

Access request flow (standard)
1. Requestor files an Access Request via the internal Form (link: /forms/access-request). Include justification, job role, duration, and resources.
2. Team lead approves or rejects within 48 business hours.
3. System owner performs second-level check for sensitive resources.
4. Security performs risk screen for privileged roles; if approved, access is provisioned.
5. Automatic expiration is set based on requested duration; renewals require re-approval.

Privileged access controls
- MFA is mandatory for all human accounts.
- Break-glass process: temporary emergency admin access requires documented justification and post-event audit within 24 hours.
- All admin activity must be logged to central audit logging (see security-and-compliance/audit-logging).

Quarterly access review
- Security runs automated inventory and sends review tasks to system owners. Owners must certify or remediate within 15 business days.

Access request template (example)
```
Access request: [Project / Service Name]
Requestor: [Full name, email]
Role requested: [Viewer | Contributor | Admin | Service Account]
Resources required: [IAM role, repo, workspace, cloud resource IDs]
Justification: [Business reason, least-privilege explanation]
Duration: [One-time | 7 days | 30 days | Permanent]
Team lead: [Name]
```

2) Change Management

Objective
Control changes that affect production and critical systems while minimizing deployment friction and enabling fast iteration.

Change categories
- Standard changes: pre-authorized routine operations with documented runbooks (minor config updates, certificate renewals).
- Normal changes: require change request, peer review, and scheduled window (releases, infra changes).
- Emergency changes: performed outside normal schedule when immediate mitigation is required. Must be documented and reviewed after the fact.

Pre-deployment checklist (for Normal changes)
- JIRA ticket submitted with rollback plan and test plan.
- Code reviewed and CI green.
- Load and smoke testing done in staging (per runtime-architecture guidance).
- Stakeholder notification (channel + email) 24–72 hours before window.

Approval matrix
- < $5k config-only or read-only changes: Team lead approval.
- Production-impacting infra changes or > $5k: Director + Platform or Security review.
- Cross-team schema changes: Product + Platform + Data owner approval.

Emergency change procedure
1. Implement mitigation and tag change as EMERGENCY with a short incident summary.
2. Notify oncall and incident responders immediately.
3. Create postmortem and change review within 5 business days.

Change request template (JIRA checklist snippet)
- Change description
- Risk assessment (Low/Medium/High)
- Rollback steps (explicit commands or playbook links)
- Test plan and acceptance criteria
- Approvers: [list]

3) Data Management

Classification
- Public: Safe for external release (docs, marketing).
- Internal: Redwood-internal usage but not sensitive.
- Sensitive: PII, customer-identifiable data, keys, or regulated datasets.
- Restricted: Highest risk (production secrets, private customer data subject to contract).

Storage & access rules
- Sensitive & Restricted data must be stored in encrypted stores and require RBAC-limited service accounts.
- Backups must follow retention policy in the table below.

Retention & backup table
| Data class | Min retention | Backup frequency | Owner |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Public | 30 days | Weekly | Document owner |
| Internal | 90 days | Daily incremental | Team owner |
| Sensitive | 1 year | Daily + offsite replication | Data owner |
| Restricted | As contract | Continuous replication | Security + Data owner |

Data handling rules
- Do not copy Restricted data to personal devices.
- Use approved tooling for dataset annotations and labeling (see applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding).
- Anonymization and masking: required before use in non-prod environments.

Periodic audits and reviews
- Data access review runs quarterly with Security and relevant data owners.
- Data retention schedules are enforced by automated lifecycle policies where supported.

Data request template (for research/test datasets)
```
Dataset request: [Purpose]
Data owner: [Team]
Data classes included: [Public/Internal/Sensitive/Restricted]
Access duration: [e.g. 30 days]
Anonymization required: [Yes/No]
Storage location (non-prod): [path or bucket]
```

4) Procurement & Expenses

Principles
- Competitive sourcing, documented approvals, and segregation of duties.
- Use company card policy and expense system for employee-paid items; prefer vendor invoicing for recurring services.

Thresholds & approvals
- <$500: Team lead approval.
- $500–$5,000: Director approval + PO where applicable.
- >$5,000: Finance + Legal review, competitive quotes (min 2), and PO before work begins.
- Recurring SaaS commitments > $10,000/year require Director-level business case and Finance sign-off.

Procurement steps (vendor/software)
1. Create Procurement Request in the procurement system with justification, budget code, and expected term.
2. Finance validates budget and issues PO if required.
3. Legal reviews contracts for terms > $5,000 or with data-processing implications.
4. Security performs risk assessment for vendor access to systems or data.
5. Vendor on-boarding checklist completed and assets inventoried.

Expense policy highlights
- Meals: per diem caps tied to location (domestic $75/day).
- Travel: receipts required for all expenses > $25.
- Non-reimbursable: personal entertainment, fines, and alcohol unless pre-approved.

Procurement request template (short)
```
Title: [Vendor / SaaS / Hardware]
Requester: [Name]
Business justification: [Value, customers affected]
Budget code: [GL acct]
Estimated cost: [$]
Term: [Monthly / Annual / One-time]
Approvers: [Team lead, Finance, Legal if required]
```

5) Vendor Management

Vendor risk tiers
- Low: Public SaaS with no access to customer data.
- Medium: Vendor with access to internal systems or non-sensitive data.
- High: Vendors with access to Restricted or customer data, or who manage infrastructure.

Onboarding checklist
- Contract executed and stored in CLM.
- Security questionnaire completed and scored.
- Data Processing Addendum (DPA) signed if applicable.
- PO and invoice terms agreed.
- Access provisioning scoped to minimum required (see Access & Permissions).

Vendor review cadence
- Low: annual review.
- Medium: semi-annual.
- High: quarterly with a detailed security and contract compliance review.

Termination steps
1. Revoke access, collect assets, and confirm data deletion or return per contract.
2. Update asset inventory and notify Finance for payment holds.
3. Close PO and archive contract.

6) Travel Policy (summary)

Booking & approvals
- Employees should use corporate travel portal for bookings.
- Manager approval required for international travel. Domestic travel requires team lead approval.

Class & per diem
- Domestic coach economy. International long-haul: premium economy with Director approval.
- Per diem covers meals and incidental expenses; receipts required for expenses above local per diem.

Safety & expense reporting
- Travel risk assessment required for Tier 2 countries (see security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention for country list).
- File expense report in the expense system within 14 days of return with receipts attached.

Emergency assistance
- 24/7 traveler assistance is available via the corporate travel program; contact details are on the travel portal.

7) Internal Templates (quick links & examples)

Included in this section are standard templates for common workflows. Teams should copy and adapt but retain required fields for auditability.

- Access request (see above)
- Procurement request (see above)
- Change request checklist (see Change Management section)
- Vendor onboarding checklist (short)

Vendor onboarding checklist (template)
```
Vendor name: []
PO number: []
Contract owner: []
Security score: []
DPA required: [Yes/No]
Services: []
Access required: []
Review cadence: [Low/Medium/High]
```

FAQ (short)
- Q: Who do I contact for an urgent access approval?
  A: Your Team lead + oncall security. Use the break-glass channel per the incident process.
- Q: How long do procurement approvals take?
  A: <$500: typically same-day. >$5K with legal review: allow 3–10 business days.

Appendix: Quick command snippets
- Revoke user via admin CLI (example):
  $ admin-cli users revoke --user user@redwood.ai --reason "Org change" --notify true

- Example rollback command (infra):
  $ deploy rollback --service runtime --to-tag v2026-11-01
